blocks.heading: Where could Arista’s shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: Arista’s weighted forecast points to $326.86 by October 2029, contingent on profitable growth as AI trials become production while customer, supply and valuation risks remain manageable. On August 4, 2026, management guided to $12,600.0 million of 2026 revenue and 40.0% growth. At least $3,500.0 million should come from AI fabrics and $1,250.0 million from campus networking. Non-GAAP gross margin is guided to 62.0%–64.0%. Operating margin is guided to 48.0%–49.0%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Arista, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The base case uses management’s $12,600M 2026 revenue guide, supported by Q2 revenue growth of 37.7%. Revenue then grows 20%, 16% and 14% across the forecast horizons. A normalized net margin of 37.5% stays below 2025’s 39.0% and near H1 2026’s 38.9%, allowing for mix and component costs.

The bear case lowers earnings to $4,868.6M in the first horizon and $5,596.5M in the last. It assumes revenue growth slows to 12% and then 8%, while margins settle near 34.0%. Two customers supplied 42% of 2025 revenue, and purchase commitments reached $9.7B, so delayed projects could weaken both absorption and margins.

The bull case reaches $6,289.9M initially and $9,676.8M by October 2029. It assumes Ethernet AI designs convert into production orders, new platforms ramp successfully and margins rise toward 40.0%. The October rack-scale announcement supports the possibility, but does not yet prove recurring revenue.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Arista really make?

paragraphs.text: Sales growth remains strong but has slowed from its earlier peak, while operating margin keeps improving. The company’s own real free cash flow fell sharply in 2022, then recovered as net cash rose; diluted EPS climbed from $0.66 in 2021 to $2.75 in 2025. The valuation is 67.8x trailing P/E against 40.9x forward P/E. Real free cash flow yield is 1.4%, and dividend yield is 0.0%.

earnings.title: Arista earnings: November 3, 2026
earnings.meta_description: Arista reports on November 3, 2026; guidance calls for strong growth, while acceptance, supply and margins are the key tests.
earnings.opening: Arista's next results are expected on November 3, 2026. Watch whether AI trials become accepted production with durable margins and cash conversion.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains Arista's business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: On August 4, 2026, Arista reported second-quarter revenue of $3,035.7 million, up 37.7% from a year earlier. It then raised its full-year revenue outlook to $12,600.0 million, or 40.0% growth. Within that total, management wants at least $3,500.0 million from AI fabrics and $1,250.0 million from campus networking. The third-quarter revenue guide is approximately $3,300.0 million.

Management also expects non-GAAP gross margin of 62.0%–64.0% and operating margin of 48.0%–49.0%. Gross margin shows what remains after the direct cost of supplying equipment; operating margin also subtracts engineering, sales and administrative costs. Non-GAAP measures exclude selected items, including stock-based compensation, so they can show operating trends but are not the same as standard accounting profit.

blocks.heading: Has Arista kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The company did meet a clear operating promise. Management forecast approximately US$8.2 billion in 2025 revenue, then reported US$9.006 billion. That is evidence of execution against a dated expectation, though exceeding revenue guidance does not automatically prove that every compensation target was demanding.

blocks.heading: What has Arista's recent revenue and profit shown?

paragraphs.text: Gross margin was 62.9% against 65.2% a year earlier. Operating margin nevertheless rose to 45.4% from 44.7%, because operating expenses grew more slowly than sales. Net income reached $1,212.9 million and diluted earnings per share reached $0.95.

blocks.heading: What should Arista watch in the next release?

paragraphs.text: The most useful update will identify what happened to the unallocated growth contribution. Investors should watch supply, inventory, customer acceptance and margins together. Rising inventory could support an approaching deployment, or it could show that components and finished equipment are waiting longer than planned. Management’s explanation should distinguish those possibilities.
